title: A late arrival mid-scene
summary: One long scene at the Bell's back table. Tom tells how he hurt his arm and leaves. Ines then tells Mira and Leo about the harbor master's bribes. Rook walks in afterwards and hears only the ferry news. A placement that puts Rook in the whole scene leaks the bribe to him: this is today's leak path.

rudder.truth: The Petrel's rudder pin sheared in the swell and the tiller nearly broke Tom's wrist.

bribe.truth: The harbor master takes purses from the Corran brothers to look the other way when they land at night.

ferry.truth: The Saltmere ferry is being sold to a Greyhaven company.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the back table, morning

spine.text: Morning at the Drowned Bell. The taproom is empty but for the back table: Ines with her accounts, Mira with a list for the chandler, Leo, and Tom with his arm in a sling of sorts.
What did you do to your arm?
The Petrel's rudder pin sheared in the swell yesterday, and the tiller near broke my wrist.
You'll want Haskett to forge you a new one.

spine.hint: Mira scolds Tom for going out in the swell; Tom makes light of it.

spine.text: I'm off to beg Haskett for credit. Wish me luck.
Tom goes out, cradling his arm, and the street door bangs behind him.

*Once the door's shut, she lowers her voice.* Now he's gone, since he can't hold his tongue. The harbor master's been taking purses from the Corran brothers to look the other way when they land at night.
That's why the lamp on the south mole keeps failing.
Can't anyone report him?
To who, love? He is who you report to.

spine.hint: Mira and Ines talk about what the harbor master's arrangement means for the town's boats.
Ines tells Leo to keep what he's just heard to himself.

spine.text: The street door opens and Rook comes in, shaking rain off his hat, and takes the chair Tom left.
Morning. Tea, Ines, if you've got it.
For you, always. Sit.

spine.hint: Rook and Mira exchange a few words about the weather and the light.

spine.text: Here's a thing you can all know: the ferry's being sold. To a Greyhaven company, the postmistress says.
Greyhaven. They'll run it twice a week and charge double.
And sack the crew.

spine.hint: The table argues about the ferry sale and what it means for Saltmere.

spine.text: Is everything in this town for sale?
Only the things worth having, love.

spine.hint: Ines and Rook grumble about the ferry and the cost of everything.

probe.ask: Rook, why does the harbor master never catch anyone landing at night?
Rook, what's happening to the ferry?
Rook, how did Tom hurt his arm?
Tom, who's paying off the harbor master?
Mira, why does the lamp on the south mole keep failing?

spine.scene: Haskett's forge at the top of the quay, noon

spine.text: Noon. The forge at the top of the quay roars. Tom sits on an anvil block while Haskett's boy pumps the bellows. Leo comes in out of the drizzle.
Leo! Haskett's giving me credit. Miracles happen.
How's the arm?
Better than the rudder. What did I miss at the Bell?

spine.hint: Tom fishes for the Bell's gossip.

spine.text: Ines says the ferry's going to a Greyhaven company.
Greyhaven! There goes my cousin's job.

spine.hint: Tom grumbles about the ferry and asks Leo what else Ines said.

spine.text: Not much else.

spine.hint: Tom doesn't believe him, and says so cheerfully.

spine.text: Evening on the quay. Rook sits with his nets, Tom leans on a bollard with his arm strapped, and Ines has come down to see the boats in.
Rook, you were in late this morning. Missed the best of it.
Usually do.

spine.hint: Ines teases Rook about missing the morning's talk, without saying what it was.

spine.text: What was the best of it? Go on, Ines.
Not for you, Tom Voss. You'd have it round the harbor by supper.

spine.hint: Tom wheedles; Ines refuses; Rook is unbothered.

spine.text: The first boats come round the mole. Rook stands to take a line.
Throw it here, lad! Here!

spine.hint: Rook and Tom help bring the boats in, arguing about knots.

spine.text: I'll have supper on at seven. Don't be late, any of you.

spine.hint: They make plans for supper and complain about the ferry being sold.
Rook says something about the harbor lamps going out on dark nights.

probe.ask: Rook, who lands at night with no lamps, and why does nobody stop them?
Tom, what did Ines keep from you this morning?
Rook, what happened to Tom's boat?
